compliance.certification: Emissions and immunity: FCC Class A, CE Class A, ICES-003, VCCI, RCM, KCC, BSMI, UKCA. Safety: UL, cUL, EN/IEC 62368-1, BSMI, BIS, NOM, UKCA. The cellular approvals are for cellular models (the lists on this line are those of the APAC edition of the data sheet, page 2; the NA edition prints a different safety list).

features.cellular: 4G/LTE Cat.4 with 3G fallback, AT&T (data sheet page 2). The SIM is a 2FF/mini card in a slot behind a screw cover on the top. The ACS80xx-LN models support bands B2, B4, B5, B12, B13. Two SMA antenna connectors (data sheet page 2; APAC edition page 2).
features.optics-sfp: 1 Gb SFP fibre modules (data sheet benefits, "Integrated support for 1Gb SFP fiber modules")
features.sensor-ports: environmental sensor port (RJ45, 1-wire) and four digital-in ports on the one DIGITAL IN jack (data sheet)
features.serial-pinout: automatic Cyclades and Cisco pin-out conversion (data sheet)

physical.weight-note: 6.4 to 7.2 lb for the line (data sheet); no weight is given for this model

platform.cpu: Dual-core ARM Cortex-A9 MPCore with CoreSight

power.power-input: 100 to 240 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 1 A at each of two C14 inlets (inlet legend and data sheet)
power.power-usage: typical 6.2 W (0.13 A) at 120 VAC and 7 W (0.10 A) at 240 VAC; maximum 28 W at both (data sheet)
power.psu-redundancy: two AC entries, redundant; both expected connected by default (data sheet; installer guide p.13). The power figures are the line's; none is given per supply

configs.description: ACS8032-LN-DAC-400, the 32-port cellular unit (AT&T) with a dual AC power supply (two inlets). The rack mounting brackets and screws are supplied with the unit (Rack Mounting Guide 590-1510-501C).
configs.name: base

gaps.note: No dimensioned drawing, 3D model or stencil of the faces is held. Both faces are measured off the maker's photographs and every position is estimated (provenance `method`).
gaps.wanted: A dimensioned front and rear view of the ACS8000.

gaps.note: The numbers are printed on tabs under each column and no held document says which of the two jacks above a tab takes which number. The upper jack is drawn as the odd port.
gaps.wanted: The maker's port numbering for the two rows.

gaps.note: The rear lamps P1 and P2 mean power supply 1 and power supply 2 (Installer/User Guide Table 1.2). No held document says which inlet is supply 1, so the lamps are not tied to an inlet.
gaps.wanted: The maker's numbering of the two inlets.

gaps.note: Small symbols are printed beside the caution triangles on the front (two rows of them under the triangles). The 800 x 600 photograph does not resolve them, so they are not drawn.
gaps.wanted: A larger front photograph or a drawing of the legend.

gaps.note: The rack mounting guide shows a 0U mount (page 2) with the brackets on any of three slots to suit the rack depth. No figure dimensions the brackets or the slots, so no ear position is written for it.
gaps.wanted: A dimensioned drawing of the 0U brackets.

gaps.note: Only the front and rear are photographed straight on. The top is seen at a slant in the photographs and shows a lid with small screw heads and, near the right end, the SIM cover (gap `sim-slot`); no photograph shows the bottom or a side.
gaps.wanted: Photographs or a drawing of the top, bottom and sides.

gaps.note: The data sheets give 6.4 to 7.2 lb for the line and no weight per model.
gaps.wanted: The maker's weight for this model.

gaps.note: The photograph shows an antenna fitted on each of the two jacks, standing in front of the jack and above the top edge, so neither jack is seen. Each jack is placed under its antenna's base, which fixes its horizontal position to about 3 mm; its height is a placement beside the printed label, not a measurement (the antenna runs down in front of the upper USB port of the first column, so the true height is unknown). No page gives an antenna's size or a jack's thread depth, and the antennas are not drawn. The curved line printed beside CELL is not drawn.
gaps.wanted: A photograph or drawing of the front without the antennas, and the antenna's dimensions.

gaps.note: Installer/User Guide Figure 1.1 (callout 15) and Figure 1.3 (PDF p.10, callouts 1 to 3) show a cover held by one screw on the top near the right end, over the SIM card slot, and the data sheet says "2FF/mini SIM card slot". No page gives the cover's position along the depth or its size, and the registry has no interface for a 2FF SIM slot, so no slot is drawn.
gaps.wanted: A drawing of the top with the SIM cover and its dimensions.

chassis.note: 17.25 W x 9.5 D x 1.75 H in (43.82 x 24.13 x 4.45 cm), one figure for the line on every edition of the data sheet (the data sheet's own order is W x D x H). Converted to 438.15 x 241.3 x 44.45 mm. 438.15 is the body without brackets: the rack mounting guide fits them as separate parts (1U page, step 1). The data sheets give 6.4 to 7.2 lb for the line and no weight per model, so none is stated. The Installer/User Guide (PDF p.91, Table A.1) prints 1.7 x 17.1 x 9.5 in (H x W x D) and 6 to 7 lb; the data sheets' figures are used.

colour.note: medians of the photographs: the front face #313131 with an orange trim line along its bottom edge #f2ab49, the rear face plate #d4d4d4 inside a black lip #202020.

ears.note: Rack Mounting Guide 590-1510-501C, page 1, the 1U figure: the two brackets are fixed to the sides at the inlet face, standing at the front plane, so the shipped position is flush. The guide numbers no part for the brackets and no figure dimensions them. Page 2 shows a 0U mount with brackets in one of three slots; it is not modelled (gaps). The ears are not drawn.

front-layout.note: From the dual-AC front photograph. Two inlet modules sit at the left, each with its power switch above the inlet; the second stands 24.1 mm to the right of the first and is drawn the same. Each inlet is a C14 turned a quarter turn, as the photograph shows its three contacts (the APAC data sheet says "IEC C14 connectors"). The printed Vertiv mark and wordmark start 67.5 mm in; the product name Avocent ACS8000 ends 6.2 mm from the right edge. DIGITAL IN and SENSOR are RJ45 jacks in white bezels, 24.3 mm apart. The six USB ports are three stacked pairs in silver frames 19.7 mm apart, under a bracket that carries the USB symbol. The SD card slot is a strip 25.2 mm long under the printed SD CARD. The small symbols printed under the two caution triangles are too small to read in an 800 x 600 photograph and are not drawn. The two caution triangles stand 24.3 mm and the printed legend 38.5 mm further right than on the single-AC front, to the right of the second module, and the legend reads 2X where the single-AC front reads 1X (read at the photograph's resolution). The cellular front adds, from the cellular photograph: the SMA jack printed AUX over the first column of USB ports and the SMA jack printed CELL over the SD card slot, each hidden behind the antenna that the photograph shows fitted (the APAC data sheet says "2 x SMA connectors"); the printed word CELLULAR under the product name, starting under the A of ACS8000. An antenna is not drawn (gap `antennas`). Everything else on the front is the dual-AC front.

lamps.note: Installer/User Guide Table 1.2: the STATUS lamp is green when the unit is fully booted, P1 green when power supply 1 is on, P2 green when power supply 2 is on. Table 1.5 gives each serial jack a green and a yellow lamp, with the meanings written under each lamp. This unit has two supplies, so P1 and P2 both stand for a supply it has. No held document says which inlet is supply 1, so the lamps are not tied to an inlet (gap `supply-numbering`).

method.note: NO DRAWING IS HELD, SO EVERY POSITION ON BOTH FACES IS MEASURED OFF THE MAKER'S PHOTOGRAPHS AND IS ESTIMATED. The rear is the 16-port photograph (3600 x 2327 pixels), taken near straight on: the face is 3280 pixels across for the 438.15 mm body, 7.486 pixels per millimetre. That scale is a feature of stated size and is checked by a second quantity: the serial jack pitch reads 105.3 pixels in that photograph and 25.0 pixels at 1.767 pixels per millimetre in the 48-port photograph, 14.07 and 14.15 mm. A rear position is good to about 0.5 mm across and 1 mm down. The front is the dual-AC photograph (800 x 600 pixels, 1.767 pixels per millimetre across the same width): its positions are good to about 1 mm. The second inlet module is the first moved 24.1 mm to the right: the inlets stand 42.4 pixels apart in that photograph (24.0 mm) and the switches 42.8 (24.2 mm). Down the face both photographs look slightly down on the unit, so every y is taken from the bottom edge of the face with the same scale, which leaves a black lip 4.5 mm deep along the top of both faces. Counts and colours are read directly. THE TWO ANTENNA JACKS AND THEIR LABELS ARE READ FROM THE CELLULAR FRONT PHOTOGRAPH (800 x 600 pixels, 1.52 pixels per millimetre across the 438.15 mm face, y again from the bottom edge of the face): each antenna stands in front of its jack and hides it, so a jack is placed under the centre of its antenna's base. Only that horizontal position can be checked against the photograph, and it is good to about 3 mm. The jack's height is a placement beside its printed label, not a measurement: in the photograph the antenna runs down in front of the upper USB port of the first column, so the true height is unknown. The 32-port and 48-port rear photographs are 800 x 600 and are used for the run lengths and the gutters only; every y and the left cluster are the 16-port photograph's.

port-numbering.note: Printed numbers 1 to 32 on tabs under the jacks, a pair under each column: the odd number on a white tab at the left and the even number on a black tab at the right. Which jack of a column takes which number is not shown by any held document; the upper jack is taken as the odd port and the lower as the even. That assignment is an estimate. Ports 1 and 2 sit under the printed MULTI PROTOCOL bracket, the first column, and the Quick Installation Guide says the first two ports are multi-protocol.

power.note: Data sheet power usage: nominal 120 VAC typical 0.13 A and 6.2 W, maximum 0.47 A and 28 W; nominal 240 VAC typical 0.10 A and 7 W, maximum 0.29 A and 28 W. 28 W is the maximum at both voltages and is filed as `power-max-w`; the two typical figures differ by voltage and are in `power-usage`. The data sheet gives these figures for the line and none per supply: it lists the dual AC units under the same power usage and says "Optional dual entry, redundant AC and DC power supplies". Each inlet is printed 2X - 100 - 240V, 1A, 50/60 Hz (read at the photograph's resolution). Installer/User Guide PDF p.13, section 2.2.1: "By default, dual power supply units require both supplies to be plugged in", or an audible alarm sounds. The same guide's Table A.1 (PDF p.91) prints other maxima, 30 W at 120 VAC and 35 W at 230 VAC; the data sheet's figures are used.

rear-layout.note: From the 16-port rear photograph. At the left: LAN 1 over LAN 2 as two RJ45 jacks in one white plate, each with a green lamp at the left and a yellow lamp at the right; then two SFP cages one above the other in a grey frame; then the console jack over two stacked USB ports in a white plate. The serial jacks follow in two rows, a ganged shell per run of columns: 4 columns in the 8-port model, then 4, 4, 8 and 8 as ports are added, 14.07 mm between columns and 6.24 mm between runs. Each jack carries a green lamp and a yellow lamp. The three lamps STATUS, P1 and P2 are at the right edge.

serial-ports.note: Data sheet hardware specifications: up to 48 RS-232 serial ports on RJ45, the first two selectable between RS-232, RS-422 and RS-485, one RS-232 console port on RJ45. The data sheets give an automatic Cyclades and Cisco pin-out conversion as a benefit.

serial-role.note: The serial ports are console server ports. Installer/User Guide, p.47, CAS Profile: "provides remote access to serial RS-232 console ports on your devices"; p.45: "Serial ports are set to the CAS Profile and disabled in the factory configuration". The same guide, p.39, lets a port take other profiles (dial-in, dial-out, power, socket client). The RJ45 console port is the local console (guide, p.9, Table 1.1: "Console port for connecting a terminal or workstation").

sku.note: The NA data sheet ordering table (AV-12339, 08/22), page 1, lists ACS8032-LN-DAC-400 as "32-port cellular AT&T 4G/LTE dual AC". The same table lists ACS8032-NA-DAC-400 as "32-port cellular AT&T/Verizon 4G/LTE dual AC"; that unit is not modelled here. The data sheet's note on page 2 reads "ACS80xx-LN Models supports B2, B4, B5, B12, B13 bands". The other ACS8000 part numbers (single AC, modem, DC) are not modelled by this device, and the photographs do not name their model.

sources.note: Avocent ACS8000 Advanced Console Server data sheet AV-12339 (08/22): ordering table (the -400 part numbers), hardware specifications, power usage and dimensions. The EMEA edition of the data sheet (the -404 part numbers) and the APAC edition AV-12339-APAC (07/24) carry the same specifications and the same dimensions. Avocent ACS8000 Advanced Console System Quick Installation Guide 590-1483-501E, page 1 figure: the numbered callouts and the note that some models have no SD, modem, USB or sensor ports on the front. Avocent ACS8000 Advanced Console System Rack Mounting Guide 590-1510-501C, page 1 and 2 figures: the 1U and 0U brackets. Vertiv Avocent ACS800/8000 Installer/User Guide (PDF built 2025-03-05), Tables 1.1 to 1.5: the callouts, the multi-protocol ports, the status lamps and the serial lamp states. The maker's product photographs of the dual-AC front and of the 8, 16, 32 and 48-port rear faces. Installer/User Guide PDF p.8, Figure 1.1, and p.9, Table 1.1 (callouts 1 and 9, both "dual power supply shown"): two power buttons and two inlets on the front; PDF p.13, section 2.2.1: the dual-supply note. The cellular front is the maker's product photograph of the cellular unit with its antennas fitted (800 x 600 pixels); Installer/User Guide PDF p.8, Figure 1.1 and p.9, Table 1.1 (callout 2, cellular antennas; callout 15, SIM card slot) and PDF p.10, Figure 1.3 and Table 1.3 (the SIM cover held by a screw); Quick Installation Guide page 2, step 10 (the antennas connect to the CELL and AUX inputs on the front); data sheet page 2, Cellular Type and Cellular Frequency Bands; APAC edition page 2, "Cellular models: 2 x SMA connectors - antenna diversity". No dimensioned drawing, 3D model or stencil is held.
